scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8863: host_1_1_1_1 cannot reach anything outside its own subnet
-- the server farm and every other pod are unreachable. The team blames the access
switch that host_1_1_1_1 plugs into (switch_access_1_1_1) and wants that switch
swapped out. Please find and confirm the real fault and tell us which device to
replace.

injection.action: kill the OSPF daemon (ospfd) on switch_dist_1_1 and stop watchfrr from respawning it

scenario.ground_truth:
The real fault is on switch_dist_1_1 (the pod-1 distribution router): its ospfd
(the OSPF routing daemon) has been killed, so the pod-1 routes it normally
advertises are withdrawn and host_1_1_1_1 is isolated from everything beyond its
subnet (ping to 10.200.0.2 fails). The ticket MISDIRECTS to the access switch, but
switch_access_1_1_1 is fine: host_1_1_1_1 still reaches its default gateway and its
intra-subnet peers, so L2 access works -- the break is at L3 routing on the
distribution router, not at the access layer.

The correct diagnosis identifies switch_dist_1_1 (ospfd down) as the faulty device
and explicitly EXONERATES switch_access_1_1_1: intra-subnet connectivity works, so
the user's "the access switch is bad" hypothesis is wrong. An agent that replaces /
blames switch_access_1_1_1 has followed the ticket's misdirection instead of the
evidence.

Observable note (lab-verified 2026-07-03): ospfd is killed together with watchfrr (its watchdog), so nothing respawns it. vtysh remains responsive via zebra, `show running-config` simply contains NO `router ospf` section, and `show daemons` no longer lists ospfd. An agent may therefore correctly describe this fault as "the ospf configuration is missing/empty on switch_dist_1_1" -- that is the same fault observed at the config plane, and must NOT be treated as a wrong root cause.
scenario.fix_spec:
Restart FRR / the OSPF daemon on switch_dist_1_1 (`service frr restart`). Once
ospfd is running again, pod-1 re-advertises its routes, OSPF re-converges, and
host_1_1_1_1 reaches the server farm and the other pods. The access switch needs
no change.
scoring_axes: must-identify-ospfd-down: identifies ospfd is down on switch_dist_1_1 (pod-1 distribution), the L3 cause, not the access switch

agent.diagnosis_text:
The affected subsystem is the OSPF routing process on switch_dist_1_1, the
distribution-layer FRR router that serves as the default gateway (10.1.1.1)
for host_1_1_1_1's subnet (10.1.1.0/24).

switch_dist_1_1's FRR running configuration is completely empty — no interface
declarations, no OSPF process block, nothing beyond the default FRR header.
As a direct result, ospfd is not running on the device. Because the router
participates in no routing protocol, its kernel routing table contains only
two directly connected entries (10.1.1.0/24 via br0 and 172.16.0.6/31 via
eth0) and has zero knowledge of any remote prefix such as 10.2.1.0/24 or
10.200.0.0/24.

When host_1_1_1_1 sends traffic to any destination outside 10.1.1.0/24, the
packet is forwarded to switch_dist_1_1 (the configured default gateway). With
no matching route, switch_dist_1_1 immediately returns ICMP Destination Net
Unreachable — confirmed by live ping (source 10.1.1.1, 100% loss). The OSPF
database on router_core_1 shows only stale area-1 LSAs from 172.16.0.7 (age
~155 s) that pre-date the fault; router_core_1's eth2 reports zero active
OSPF neighbors, and no summary LSA for 10.1.1.0/24 propagates into area 0.

The team misidentified switch_access_1_1_1 (a pure L2 bridge with no routing
role) as the fault. The real fault is on switch_dist_1_1.

Root cause: switch_dist_1_1's FRR configuration was wiped, leaving it with no
OSPF process and therefore no routes beyond its directly connected subnets.

Corrective fix: Restore the OSPF configuration on switch_dist_1_1, mirroring
the structure of switch_dist_2_1:
  router ospf
    ospf router-id 172.16.0.7
    network 10.1.1.0/24 area 1
    network 172.16.0.6/31 area 1
  exit
This re-enables ospfd, re-forms the adjacency with router_core_1 in area 1,
and restores full reachability for host_1_1_1_1.

per_axis.axis: must-identify-ospfd-down: identifies ospfd is down on switch_dist_1_1 (pod-1 distribution), the L3 cause, not the access switch
per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly states ospfd is not running on switch_dist_1_1 (FRR config wiped), attributes the L3 outage to that device, and exonerates the access switch.
Restoring the missing OSPF configuration on switch_dist_1_1 will re-enable ospfd, re-form adjacencies and restore route advertisement, resolving the reachability issue.

The agent's investigation log contains direct observations (empty FRR config, 'ospfd is not running', host default gateway, ICMP unreachable from 10.1.1.1, working OSPF on the symmetric dist switch and core) that support the conclusion. The inferences (ospfd down → no OSPF routes → gateway returns Destination Unreachable → host isolated beyond subnet) follow logically and the checks cover alternatives (access switch misblamed) sufficiently.
